phases.name: Foundations
phases.scope: Monorepo, Compose (two databases), ledger, idempotency, FSM and outbox kits, auditor skeleton, banksim accounts
phases.exit_gate: M1–M4, M6 properties; CC1 at ledger level

phases.name: Pay wallet core
phases.scope: Customers, PIN, OTP, linking, cash-in, cash-out, P2P, limits, freeze, surplus floor, escrow reconciliation
phases.exit_gate: W1–W3; CC2, CC5, CC8–CC10; C1, C10

phases.name: Pay merchant payments
phases.scope: Payment Intents (wallet and card), card authorize/capture/void/refund, disputes, webhooks, incoming sweep, card pending funds, settlement, funding, disbursements, card top-ups and chargebacks, PSP reconciliation

phases.name: Tickets on-sale
phases.scope: Events, seat maps, waiting room, inventory, Redis filter, reservations, checkout through Pay, asynchronous saga with capture-refusal compensation, tickets

phases.name: Tickets money
phases.scope: Fees, refunds, disputes, event cancellation with pre-funding, organizer funds release and payouts, Pay settlement reconciliation

phases.name: Resale
phases.scope: Listings, locks, sale commit and ownership transfer, resale payments, seller proceeds and disbursements, resale disputes, cancellation with resale chains

phases.name: Proof under load
phases.scope: End-to-end k6 scenarios, chaos suite, hot-account benchmarks, SERIALIZABLE comparison

phases.name: Hardening
phases.scope: Dashboards, ADR files, runbooks, README, demo
phases.exit_gate: A fresh clone runs `task demo` end to end

items.title: Repository skeleton: go.mod, layout, Taskfile, lint
items.done_when: go.mod (Go >= 1.25) and the TD §2 directory layout exist; Taskfile.yml has check (build, vet, golangci-lint, govulncheck, unit tests, go run scripts/brief/main.go -check; prints failures only), test (the full suite), up, down, migrate and chaos; golangci-lint enables the rules ENGINEERING.md marks lint; task check passes on the skeleton; AGENTS.md › Conventions lists the commands.

evidence.review: reviewer CHANGES NEEDED, 0 blockers; major (E9/E13/E28 lint-only gaps) fixed by D13 in 4ddf130, minors fixed in af91eb6 or recorded in the report

items.title: Local stack: Compose with two PostgreSQL databases and Redis; migrations
items.done_when: task up starts PostgreSQL >= 17 with databases bastion_pay and bastion_tickets (track_commit_timestamp = on) and Redis >= 7.2; task migrate applies db/pay and db/tickets migrations; application roles pay_app and tickets_app exist; an integration test connects to both databases and to Redis.

items.title: Platform basics: money, ids, config, transactions, logging
items.done_when: money: int64 minor units, basis points as floor(amount × bps / 10 000) with the 9.2 × 10^14 bound, no floating point; ids: UUIDv7; config loads the TD §33 variables needed so far; db: pgx pool and a transaction helper that retries 40001/40P01 up to 3 times with jitter and maps SQLSTATEs per TD §1.5; logx: slog JSON. Unit tests cover the money bounds and the error mapping.

items.title: Architecture test for module boundaries
items.done_when: internal/archtest fails when pay/** and tickets/** import each other, when audit imports anything but platform, or when simulators import product code; a test proves each rule fails on a violating fixture.

items.title: Ledger kit: schema, triggers and privileges
items.done_when: The TD §3.1 schema and triggers exist in both databases; integration tests show: an unbalanced entry fails at commit (M1); balances change only through the triggers and the application role cannot update balance columns (M2); UPDATE and DELETE on entries, postings, resolutions and seals are rejected (M3); within_bound rejects a bound violation with 23514 (M4); a second entry with the same (kind, reference_id) fails with 23505 (M6).

items.title: Ledger kit: Go API (Batch Lock, Post, Resolve, Flush)
items.done_when: The TD §3.3 API: one Batch per transaction; Flush validates sum = 0 and two-legged holds, resolves shards and lazy owner accounts, locks all accounts once ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE, inserts sorted by account, inserts unsealed, maps 23514 to ErrBoundViolated and 23505 to ErrAlreadyPosted; a hold resolves once (POSTED <= held, VOIDED, EXPIRED) and a second resolution returns ErrAlreadyResolved. Integration tests cover each path.

items.title: Ledger sealer and chain verification
items.done_when: The sealer (250 ms singleton) appends (entry_hash, chain_hash) in sealing order outside the write transaction; a verifier re-hashes the chain; a tamper test (an edit as superuser) breaks the chain at exactly the edited seq.

items.title: Ledger property tests (M1, M2, M4, M6)
items.done_when: rapid property tests over random sequences of posts, holds and resolutions, including duplicates and bound violations, keep M1, M2 (balances recomputed from postings), M4 and M6 after every step; fixed seeds in CI. M3 is covered by the integration and tamper tests of P1-05 and P1-07 (INV §10.3).

items.title: CC1 at ledger level: concurrent transfers in both directions
items.done_when: 1,000 concurrent transfers in both directions between the same accounts through the ledger kit, under -race against real PostgreSQL: no deadlock, every balance exact, M1 and M2 hold afterwards.

items.title: Idempotency kit
items.done_when: TD §4.1 schema and §4.2 protocol: scope, fingerprint (SHA-256 of method, path and JCS body), 30 s lease, the decision table (422 on hash mismatch; replay with Idempotent-Replayed; 409 with Retry-After or Location; guarded takeover of an expired lease), completion in the transaction of the deterministic outcome, claim deleted when nothing durable happened, transient failures never stored; derived-key helpers for TD §4.3. 100 identical concurrent requests give exactly one winner and one effect.

items.title: State machine kit
items.done_when: fsm.states and fsm.edges; trigger fsm.guard(object_type) rejects illegal initial states and edges with P0001 illegal_transition and appends fsm.state_events; a test checks the Go mirror of each graph against the database; guarded UPDATE helpers turn stale transitions into counted no-ops.

items.title: Outbox, relay and inbox
items.done_when: Outbox rows written in the producing transaction; one relay per database publishes to the product's Redis stream at least once (marks after XADD); consumers commit the effect and outbox.inbox (consumer, event_id) together and XACK after commit; XAUTOCLAIM after 60 s; DLQ after 5 deliveries. Tests: a relay killed mid-batch republishes without loss; duplicate deliveries apply once.

items.title: banksim: accounts
items.done_when: banksim holds accounts with owner national IDs and balances, seeded with acct_ok, acct_fail, acct_return_after_10s, acct_timeout_after_accept and acct_insufficient; money only moves between accounts, so the total is conserved. Operations, statements and webhooks come with P2-07.

items.title: Auditor skeleton with ledger checks
items.done_when: internal/audit imports platform only and reads both databases with read-only roles; runs the M1–M4 Detect queries of INV in short REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshots at the TD §31 intervals; exposes GET /report[?quiesce=], GET /status and bastion_invariant_violations{product,code}; a clean run reports zero, and a row corrupted as superuser is reported by the matching check.

items.title: Phase 1 exit gate
items.done_when: Every Phase 1 item is done; one full run passes the M1, M2, M4, M6 properties, the M3 integration and tamper tests and CC1 at ledger level under -race, with zero auditor violations afterwards. Then set phase 1 to done and review the Phase 2 items with the owner.

items.title: Pay chart of accounts and entry templates
items.done_when: The Pay accounts of TD §9.1 (codes, normal sides, lower bounds, shards for unbounded hot accounts) and the entry templates of §9.2 exist as code over the ledger kit; a test per template proves it balances (M1) and reproduces the worked examples of §9.3.

items.title: Job runner and kit housekeeping jobs
items.done_when: platform/jobs runs PostgreSQL-native loops: singletons, and SKIP LOCKED workers with leases and next_attempt_at, stopped through context; ledger-sealer, ledger-pending-expirer, idempotency-gc and outbox-gc run on it at their TD §18.2 cadences; a worker killed while holding a lease has its work taken over after the lease expires (S7).

items.title: Incoming webhooks kit (kit/webhookin)
items.done_when: X-Signature (t=…, v1=HMAC-SHA256) checked against every active secret; |now − t| > 5 min rejected; the inbox insert, the recorder's guarded changes and its ledger batch commit in one transaction; duplicates return 200 with no effect; stale transitions are counted no-ops (webhook_stale_total); errors return 500 so the sender retries.

items.title: Chaos harness
items.done_when: test/chaos (build tag chaos) starts Compose with the chaos profile, injects faults through Toxiproxy, docker kill and failpoints (BASTION_FAILPOINTS, build tag failpoints), drives traffic, and asserts zero violations from the auditor's /report?quiesce=60s plus scenario checks; task chaos -- <code> runs one scenario.

items.title: Customers and wallets: registration, state machine, freeze
items.done_when: Registration with a unique phone number; the wallet starts PENDING_VERIFICATION and can neither send nor receive; the TD §10.1 wallet state machine runs through kit/fsm; ops freeze, unfreeze and close with an audit log; a frozen wallet rejects customer-initiated debits (wallet guard under the share lock, lock level 3) and accepts credits.

items.title: PIN
items.done_when: A 6-digit PIN stored only as an Argon2id hash with the TD §33 parameters and required for every customer-initiated debit; five consecutive wrong PINs lock debits for 30 minutes; the counter lives in its own short transaction (TD §18.1); CC9: 50 concurrent wrong-PIN attempts give at most 5 verifications.

items.title: banksim: verifications, debits, transfers, statements, webhooks, faults
items.done_when: POST /v1/verifications (holder check, mandate after a simulated bank OTP), /v1/debits (succeeded, accepted or insufficient_funds), /v1/transfers (later paid, failed or returned), GET /v1/operations?idempotency_key=, daily statements; signed webhooks debit.*, transfer.paid|failed|returned, account.credited; the test accounts behave as named; seeded faults (timeouts after accept, duplicated and reordered webhooks, corrupted statements); one effect per idempotency key; statements agree with balances unless a corruption fault is set.

items.title: OTP and bank linking
items.done_when: OTP: 5 minutes, 3 attempts, single use, required for linking and cash-out; linking verifies with banksim that the account holder is the wallet holder (key verify:{link}, three-phase call, unknown outcome resolved by lookup with the same key); the wallet becomes ACTIVE only after the first verified link; bank money moves only through the holder's verified accounts (W3).

items.title: Limits
items.done_when: Daily and monthly usage rows guarded by CHECK within_cap, with periods from the database clock in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, locked DAY before MONTH (lock level 4); P2P sends count, incoming money and card payments do not; reserve, convert and release operations exist for wallet payments (used by P3-04); tests cross day and month boundaries.

items.title: Cash-in and the bank-operation resolver
items.done_when: Cash-in debits the verified linked account into escrow with key cashin:{id} (three-phase call); the wallet is credited only after the bank confirms (webhook or lookup); unknown outcomes are explicit states resolved by pay-resolver with the same key; C1: the bank times out after debiting, there is one debit and the wallet is credited once.

items.title: Cash-out
items.done_when: OTP and PIN; only to a verified linked account of the holder; the amount is held at creation, settled when paid, released on failure and re-credited on return; key cashout:{id}; C10 for cash-outs: a transfer that times out after acceptance happens once per key, and a returned transfer is re-credited.

items.title: P2P transfers
items.done_when: ACTIVE to ACTIVE by phone number, confirmed by PIN, atomic and instant in one transaction with one ledger batch and locks in the TD §18.1 order; CC1: 1,000 concurrent transfers in both directions, no deadlock, balances exact; CC5: 50 concurrent debits exceeding one wallet's balance never drive it negative; CC8 (transfers): 20 concurrent transfers at the monthly cap at 23:59:59 and month end never exceed it; CC10: a freeze racing 100 debits, no debit after the freeze.
items.notes: CC1 through P2P is proposed here; the owner confirms (open question in NOW.md).

items.title: Safeguarding accounts and the surplus floor
items.done_when: Escrow and operating accounts at the bank (TD §17.1); the surplus_floor row (lock level 5) maintained conservatively per §17.2 and never negative (S15); operations that let e-wallet balances run ahead of escrow money are refused when the surplus is insufficient; initial capital (PAY_INITIAL_CAPITAL) injected through bastionctl inject-capital.

items.title: Escrow statement reconciliation and the daily W1 proof
items.done_when: bank-statement-importer matches every escrow statement line to the ledger; the bank-confirmed closing balance is proven to cover all e-wallet balances at the cut-off (W1); safeguarding-trueup runs after statements; every difference becomes an exception with a reason, resolved by ops with an audit trail.

items.title: Pay customer API
items.done_when: The TD §29.2 endpoints for registration, PIN, OTP, linking, cash-in, cash-out, P2P, balances, holds, remaining limits and statements; every money-moving endpoint requires Idempotency-Key (400 if missing, replay, 422 on mismatch, 409 while in progress); RFC 9457 problem types (§29.6); server deadlines; CC2 (P2P): 100 identical concurrent P2P requests make one transfer.

items.title: Auditor: Pay wallet checks
items.done_when: The auditor runs W2 (5 s), W3 (30 s) and W1 (after each statement) on bastion_pay, plus S3, S7, S8, S9, S10 and S15; each check reports a row corrupted as superuser and stays at zero on a clean run; /status exposes pay.wallets_ok.

items.title: Pay model-based test: wallets, limits, funding, P2P
items.done_when: A rapid state-machine test drives random sequences of registration, linking, cash-in, cash-out (with bank failures and returns), P2P, freezes and limit-period changes against a reference model, checking W1–W3 and M1–M4 after every step; fixed seeds in CI.

items.title: Phase 2 exit gate
items.done_when: Every Phase 2 item is done; one full run passes W1–W3 (model and property tests), CC2, CC5, CC8, CC9 and CC10 under -race, and chaos C1 and C10, with zero auditor violations. Then set phase 2 to done and review the Phase 3 items with the owner.

items.title: pspsim: card network simulator
items.done_when: The TD §30.1 endpoints, tokens and seeded faults; the contract holds: a declined authorization never becomes authorized, a final capture refusal never becomes a capture, a void answered voided or expired is final, a dispute never exceeds captured minus refunds accepted before it; signed webhooks; settlement files with the §30.1 line types; lookup by idempotency key.

items.title: Merchants: onboarding, API keys, webhook secrets, merchant accounts
items.done_when: Merchants onboarded through the ops API with API keys and rotatable webhook secrets; merchant ledger accounts per TD §9.1: sharded MERCHANT_INCOMING, MERCHANT_CARD_PENDING, MERCHANT_BALANCE bounded at −refund_credit_limit, MERCHANT_DEBT.

items.title: Payment Intents: create, state machine, cancel and expiry
items.done_when: Create with amount, currency, merchant reference, allowed methods and confirmation deadline, manual capture; at most one non-cancelled intent per merchant reference; the TD §14.1 state machine through kit/fsm; cancel before capture; intent-expirer; confirmation, capture, cancellation and expiry racing each other have exactly one winner (concurrency test); every object retrievable by its idempotency key.

items.title: Wallet confirmation and capture
items.done_when: Checks wallet status, PIN, balance and limits, then places a two-phase hold; the limit is reserved at authorization, converted at capture and released on cancel; capture once, at most the authorized amount, MDR charged at capture per method; CC8 extended to wallet confirmations at the monthly cap.

items.title: Card confirmation: attempts, authorization, resolver
items.done_when: Each card attempt has an attempt_seq with partial unique indexes (at most one live attempt per intent); authorization key auth:{intent}:{attempt}; outcomes are recorded on the operation row first, so stale or duplicate messages about an earlier attempt never change the intent; a timeout never starts a second authorization: card-operation-resolver looks up with the same key; failed confirmations follow FR-PPI-04; C17 and C20 pass.

items.title: Card capture and void
items.done_when: Capture once, at most the authorized amount, never within 1 hour of the authorization's expiry; processing answers followed to completion; a final refusal voids the authorization; a refusal the network retries stays pending until its outcome; uncaptured authorizations are cancelled after the capture window; void outcomes voided or expired are final.

items.title: Refunds
items.done_when: Full or partial refunds any number of times, never above captured minus disputed; held against availability when created; wallet refunds instant; card refunds asynchronous with key refund:{id}, failures handled; MDR not returned.

items.title: Disputes and merchant debt
items.done_when: dispute.created debits the merchant balance for the amount plus the dispute fee; any part beyond the refund credit limit becomes MERCHANT_DEBT, repaid from future captures; evidence forwarded until the deadline (dispute-deadline job); a won dispute reverses the amount but not the fee; a lost one is final; refunded plus disputed never exceeds captured.

items.title: Incoming sweep and pending card funds
items.done_when: Wallet captures land in sharded MERCHANT_INCOMING and incoming-sweeper moves them to MERCHANT_BALANCE within seconds (S1); card captures stay in MERCHANT_CARD_PENDING until settled (S18; release in P3-14).

items.title: Merchant webhook delivery
items.done_when: Every merchant-visible change inserts an event and a PENDING delivery in the same transaction; webhook-dispatcher claims due deliveries (SKIP LOCKED, at most 16 in flight per merchant), signs with every active secret, retries on the TD §16 schedule with ±20% jitter, FAILED after 72 h, ops replay; C9: the relay or the dispatcher killed after sending, before marking, leaves duplicates that receivers deduplicate.

items.title: Merchant settlement
items.done_when: The daily settlement-batcher holds the available balance above the settlement reserve (at least the minimum) and settlement-processor transfers it with key settlement:{id} and a settlement report; failures release, returns re-credit; C10 for settlements.

items.title: Merchant funding and disbursements
items.done_when: Pre-funding by bank transfer carrying a Pay reference (funding-expirer for unmatched fundings); disbursements to a customer wallet by phone number, checked available >= amount under the account lock, never credit; recipient lookup returns the masked holder name; one disbursement per merchant reference.

items.title: Card top-ups and top-up chargebacks
items.done_when: Top-ups charge a card token with key topup:{id} and credit the wallet on success only within the safeguarding buffer, refused when the surplus floor is used; a chargeback takes the amount back, any shortfall becomes CUSTOMER_DEBT, the wallet is frozen and later cash-ins repay the debt first; C15 passes.

items.title: PSP settlement reconciliation and card funds release
items.done_when: psp-settlement-importer matches every settlement line (CHARGE, CAPTURE, REFUND, CHARGEBACK, CHARGEBACK_REVERSAL, FEE, DISPUTE_FEE) to top-ups, captures, refunds and disputes; matched captures release the merchant's pending card funds; every difference becomes an exception (M7); S6 and S18 hold; CC11: 5,000 concurrent captures (wallet and card) for one merchant leave exact balances after sweep and release; C16 passes.

items.title: Incoming PSP and bank webhooks at Pay (C2, Pay side)
items.done_when: Every PSP and bank webhook Pay consumes goes through kit/webhookin; C2 for PSP → Pay and bank → Pay: webhooks duplicated 3× and reordered cause no regression and one effect per event (Pay → Tickets is added in P4-13).

items.title: Pay merchant and ops API
items.done_when: The TD §29.3 merchant endpoints (intents, confirmations, capture, cancel, refunds, disputes and evidence, funding, disbursements with recipient lookup, settlements) and the §29.4 ops endpoints; idempotency on every mutating endpoint; the §29.7 end-to-end card example runs as a test; CC2 for wallet and card confirmations and captures.

items.title: Auditor: Pay payment checks
items.done_when: M5, M6 (tripwires on every unique key INV M6 lists for Pay), M7 after each file, and S1, S4, S6, S9 and S18 on bastion_pay; each reports a corrupted row and stays at zero on a clean run.

items.title: Pay model extended to merchant payments
items.done_when: The Pay model adds wallet and card intents, refunds, disputes, debt, pending card funds, settlements, disbursements and the surplus floor; M1–M7 and W1–W3 hold after every step; fixed seeds in CI.

items.title: Phase 3 exit gate
items.done_when: Every Phase 3 item is done; one full run passes M5 and M7 for Pay, CC11 under -race, and chaos C2, C9, C15, C16, C17 and C20, with zero auditor violations. Then set phase 3 to done and review the Phase 4 items with the owner.

items.title: Tickets schemas, chart of accounts and entry templates
items.done_when: bastion_tickets schemas and roles per TD §19.1; the accounts of §20.1 and the entry templates of §20.2 exist as code over the ledger kit; a test per template proves it balances and reproduces the worked examples of §20.3.

items.title: Catalog: events, zones, seat maps, lifecycle
items.done_when: Organizers create draft events with GA or SEATED zones and seat maps whose seat counts equal capacities; ops publishes and sets the service fee; published data is immutable except zone suspension; event-scheduler moves events through pre-queue, on-sale, sales closed and completed; public availability is at most 2 s stale.

items.title: Inventory in PostgreSQL: zones, seats, fan quota
items.done_when: The PostgreSQL operations of TD §23.1 with guarded updates and CHECKs: zone counters, seats with at most one live ticket, fan quota with CHECK within_limit; seat pick holds exactly the requested seats; best available never waits on other fans' seats; locks in the TD §28.1 order.

items.title: Redis admission filter and inventory reconciler
items.done_when: The Redis keys of §23.3 and the Lua scripts admit, confirm, giveback_claim and giveback_reservation (§23.4–§23.5); sold-out and over-limit requests are rejected without touching PostgreSQL; inventory-reconciler rebuilds Redis from PostgreSQL; the safety argument of §23.7 is covered by tests; C7: FLUSHALL mid on-sale, no oversell, rebuilt within 5 s.

items.title: Waiting room
items.done_when: One signed queue ticket per fan and event; pre-queue fans shuffled at on-sale time, FIFO after; position independent of polling; wr-controller admits by measured goodput and latency and never beyond what the remaining inventory can serve; admission tokens per §22.5; admission freezes on an I or X violation (auditor /status); reservations without a valid token get a problem pointing to the waiting room; fairness measured per §22.6.

items.title: Reservations: Tx A, admit, Tx B, expiry
items.done_when: Tx A → admit → Tx B per §24.2, all-or-nothing across items; the per-fan limit counts held, purchased and resale-purchased tickets; reservations expire after 8 minutes and reservation-expirer releases them within 5 s; CC3 (5,000 fans, 1,000 GA tickets: exactly 1,000), CC4 (one fan, 10 parallel reservations, limit 4: exactly 4), CC7 (seat contention: one winner per seat, no deadlock) and C3 (kill -9 between admit and Tx B: no PostgreSQL effect, Redis restored) pass.

items.title: Pay client with derived keys and breaker
items.done_when: tickets/payments/payclient is the only way Tickets reaches Pay (archtest); derived keys per TD §4.3; outcome classes of §6.2 recorded; retry budget and breaker of §6.3; C11 (Pay brownout, 60% errors and +500 ms): the breaker opens, reservations are kept, no 5xx storm.

items.title: Checkout: Tx A′, Tx C, Pay, Tx D
items.done_when: Per §24.4: one Payment Intent per order (created or returned), wallet and card allowed, confirmation deadline 30 s before the reservation ends; checkout extends the reservation so 4 minutes remain, never beyond 12 minutes in total.

items.title: Authorization and commit: Tx R, Tx E
items.done_when: Tx R records the authorization; Tx E commits every reservation of the order while it is valid, otherwise the intent is cancelled; the expirer and Tx E have exactly one winner (opposite time guards, I4); C4: an authorization arriving after the countdown leaves the reservation expired, the intent cancelled and no tickets.

items.title: Capture and ticket issuance: Tx F, capture, Tx G
items.done_when: Exactly the order total is captured; tickets are issued in the transaction that records the capture, one per unit, seated tickets naming their seat; the QR payload is signed with a rotatable key and carries the owner version; asynchronous captures are followed to a terminal outcome; C14 (partition during capture): one capture, tickets issued once.

items.title: Capture refusal and the cancel path (Tx X)
items.done_when: Final refusal: authorization voided, seats back on sale, no tickets, fan not charged, no manual step; refusal retried by the network: order completed once, seats never released; capture_after_cancel: no state change, a CAPTURE_AFTER_CANCEL exception (M7a); Tx X uncommits only on payment_intent.canceled; C21 (a), (b) and (c) pass.

items.title: Saga recovery: payment-driver, intent-poller, tickets-resolver
items.done_when: Every row of the recovery matrix (§24.10) has a test; late or lost webhooks are covered by polling; C12 (kill -9 at every saga step in both products): terminal within 60 s, at most one effect per key at every partner; C6 (both PostgreSQL databases restart during a burst): everything terminal within 60 s after restart.

items.title: Pay webhooks at Tickets (C2 complete)
items.done_when: Pay → Tickets webhooks are consumed through kit/webhookin, with polling as backup; C2 complete: PSP → Pay, bank → Pay and Pay → Tickets webhooks duplicated 3× and reordered cause no regression and one effect per event.

items.title: Tickets API
items.done_when: The TD §29.5 endpoints for the public catalog and availability, the waiting room, reservations, checkout, orders and tickets, organizers and ops; idempotency on every endpoint that moves seats, money or tickets; CC2 for reservations and checkouts.

items.title: Auditor: Tickets ledger, inventory and X1 checks
items.done_when: M1–M4 on bastion_tickets; I1 and I3 (5 s); I2, I4 and X1 (30 s, X1 with its 5 min grace); I2 Redis convergence in quiesce mode; S5 and S14; /status exposes tickets.inventory_ok and by_event for the admission kill switch; each check reports a corrupted row and stays at zero on a clean run.

items.title: Tickets model and the joint Pay–Tickets model
items.done_when: A Tickets model (seats, quotas, orders, tickets, owners) and the Pay and Tickets models together through a fake HTTP boundary; I1–I4 and X1 hold after every step; fixed seeds in CI.

items.title: Phase 4 exit gate
items.done_when: Every Phase 4 item is done; one full run passes I1–I4 and X1, CC3, CC4 and CC7 under -race, and chaos C3, C4, C6, C7, C11, C12, C14 and C21, with zero auditor violations. Then set phase 4 to done and review the Phase 5 items with the owner.

items.title: Fees and the primary split
items.done_when: Per ticket: commission = floor(face × bps / 10 000), organizer net = face − commission, platform = commission + service fee; MDR and dispute fees booked as platform costs; S11 formulas hold.

items.title: Refunds
items.done_when: Organizers or ops refund specific valid tickets (face value + service fee), at most once per ticket; tickets are REFUND_PENDING during the refund and VOID once refunded; organizer-requested refunds respect the overdraft limit; refund-processor is rate-limited; S12 holds; C5 (concurrent refunds of the same tickets, and of different tickets exceeding the capture): one per ticket, sum within captured at both companies.

items.title: Disputes at Tickets (primary payments)
items.done_when: On a dispute: the disputed tickets still owned by the payer are revoked, platform fees reversed, the net recovered from the organizer and the rest booked as credit losses; evidence submitted through Pay (dispute-evidence); won: tickets reinstated and recoveries reversed (not the dispute fee); lost: primary tickets voided; S12 holds.

items.title: Funding Bastion Pay
items.done_when: When Tickets' balance at Pay cannot cover refunds, Tickets pre-funds it (bank transfer key fundxfer:{funding}, Pay funding key funding:{funding}); refunds wait as AWAITING_FUNDS until the funds arrive, then proceed.

items.title: Event cancellation (primary payments)
items.done_when: Cancellation stops admission, cancels open intents, voids every ticket and refunds every primary payment independently and in any order from money held for that sale, pre-funding Pay when needed; the event-cancellation job is rate-limited; S13 holds 24 h after cancellation.

items.title: Organizer funds release and payouts
items.done_when: Organizer funds stay held until the show has ended plus TIX_PAYOUT_DELAY_DAYS; organizer-funds-release, the daily organizer-payout-batcher and organizer-payout-processor pay by bank transfer with key payout:{id}; S2 and S17 hold; CC6 (payouts racing refunds and disputes): bounds hold; C10 for organizer payouts.

items.title: Pay settlement reconciliation at Tickets
items.done_when: pay-settlement-importer reconciles every Bastion Pay settlement report and bank-statement-importer Tickets' own statement; every difference is explained; S16 holds when quiescent; C8 (corrupted PSP file, escrow statement and Pay settlement report): every difference explained, M7 identities hold.

items.title: Auditor: Tickets money checks
items.done_when: M7 for Tickets, S2, S11, S12, S13, S16 and S17 run at their TD §31 cadences; each reports a corrupted row and stays at zero on a clean run.

items.title: Phase 5 exit gate
items.done_when: Every Phase 5 item is done; one full run passes M7 for Tickets, CC6 under -race, and chaos C5 and C8, with zero auditor violations. Then set phase 5 to done and review the Phase 6 items with the owner.

items.title: Listings: list, withdraw, expire
items.done_when: The owner of a VALID ticket lists it at a price <= face (CHECK price_cap) with a verified Pay payout phone until 2 h before the show; at most one open listing per ticket; listed tickets cannot be refunded, transferred elsewhere or used for entry; withdrawing locks the listing before the ticket (§28.1); listing-expirer closes listings at the cut-off.

items.title: Listing lock and the lock sweeper
items.done_when: Buying locks the listing for one buyer for 8 minutes; concurrent buyers get exactly one winner; the seller cannot withdraw a locked listing; resale purchases count toward the buyer's per-fan limit and leave the seller's; listing-lock-sweeper releases expired locks (S14).

items.title: Resale commit, capture and ownership transfer (Tx E, Tx G)
items.done_when: On authorization, Tx E sets the listing LOCKED → SELLING only while the lock is valid, otherwise the authorization is voided; Tx G records the capture and transfers ownership atomically (new owner, new owner_version, transfer row) with the seller credit; a refused capture cancels the sale; CC12 (500 buyers lock the same listing while the seller withdraws; 1,000 listings bought concurrently): one outcome per listing, one owner per ticket; C19 (the lock expires as the authorization arrives): exactly one outcome.

items.title: Seller proceeds and payouts
items.done_when: Seller proceeds = price − resale fee (5%, rounded down); the buyer pays price + service fee; proceeds held in SELLER_PAYABLE until the show has ended plus the payout delay, then disbursed through Bastion Pay (key disburse:{payout}) by seller-payouts; S17 holds.

items.title: Resale disputes and the single-hop unwind
items.done_when: A dispute on a resold primary ticket keeps the ticket with the buyer and recovers the payer's proceeds; a lost resale dispute while the buyer still owns the ticket returns it to the seller in one hop (UNWIND), except for a cancelled event; a dispute wins over an uncommitted resale of the payer's ticket (listing cancelled, buyer's authorization voided) and waits for a committed one (Tickets answers 409 while SELLING, Pay redelivers); C18 and C22 pass.

items.title: Event cancellation with resale chains
items.done_when: Cancellation also cancels listings; every resale buyer is refunded from the held proceeds of the sale they bought from, independently of every other refund; ownership is never unwound; C13 (chains A → B → C after settlement, random completion order, one card refund failing once): every ticket VOID, every payment refunded exactly once, every fan's net 0, no UNWIND transfer.

items.title: Auditor and models for resale
items.done_when: The auditor checks I5 and X2 (30 s), and S14 and S17 for resale; the Tickets model adds listings, owners and seller balances; I3, I5 and X2 hold after every step.

items.title: Phase 6 exit gate
items.done_when: Every Phase 6 item is done; one full run passes I5 and X2, CC12 under -race, and chaos C13, C18, C19 and C22, with zero auditor violations. Then set phase 6 to done and review the Phase 7 items with the owner.

items.title: Full chaos suite C1–C22
items.done_when: All 22 chaos scenarios run from test/chaos with zero violations; the PR subset (C1, C2, C4, C5, C14, C17, C20, C21) and the nightly full suite are wired into the task runner, and into CI once it exists.

items.title: Load: wallet_mixed and safeguarding_stress
items.done_when: The k6 arrival-rate scenarios wallet_mixed and safeguarding_stress meet their TD §34.3 assertions with zero violations; each run writes docs/benchmarks/YYYY-MM-DD-<scenario>.md with environment, versions, seeds, configuration, k6 summary, auditor report and conclusions.

items.title: Load: onsale_burst and fairness
items.done_when: onsale_burst (50,000 fans in 60 s, wallet and card, expiries and retries): sold <= capacity, no seat twice, tickets = paid units, p99 targets of PRD §10.2 met or deviations documented; fairness report per PRD §11; report in docs/benchmarks.

items.title: Load: resale_rush, pay_brownout, cancellation_refunds
items.done_when: resale_rush, pay_brownout and cancellation_refunds meet their TD §34.3 assertions with zero violations; reports in docs/benchmarks.

items.title: Hot-account benchmarks and SERIALIZABLE comparison
items.done_when: Benchmarks of the sharded merchant incoming account against a single hot row, and of READ COMMITTED with guarded updates against SERIALIZABLE on the hot paths, with reports and conclusions in docs/benchmarks.
items.notes: The task names hot_accounts and serializable are placeholders until the scenarios exist.

items.title: Phase 7 exit gate
items.done_when: Every Phase 7 item is done; all invariants hold under load and chaos; every PRD §10.2 target is met or its deviation documented with measurements; the reports are published in docs/benchmarks. Then set phase 7 to done and review the Phase 8 items with the owner.

items.title: Observability: metrics, traces, logs, dashboards
items.done_when: The TD §32 metrics are exported; traces propagate Tickets → Pay → card network and back through webhooks; slog JSON with IDs and none of the secrets §32 lists (a test checks the logs); the dashboards Bastion Pay, On-sale live, Resale, Refunds/disputes/cancellations and Ledgers and audit are provisioned in Grafana.

items.title: bastionctl
items.done_when: Every TD §35.2 command is implemented and tested; ops actions are audit-logged.

items.title: Alerts and runbooks
items.done_when: Every TD §35.3 alert exists as a Prometheus rule with its runbook; kill switches follow INV §11; the rules pass validation.

items.title: ADR files
items.done_when: Each AD of ARCH §10 has its own file in docs/adr/, and ARCH §10 links to them.

items.title: README and demo
items.done_when: The README explains the project and how to run it; task demo seeds bank accounts and customers, cashes in, runs a short on-sale with wallet and card, resells tickets, disputes one card payment, cancels a second event with resales, and prints the safeguarding and auditor reports.

items.title: Phase 8 exit gate
items.done_when: Every Phase 8 item is done; a fresh clone runs task demo end to end with zero auditor violations.
